summary: axios typosquat routes every GET through a third-party 'telemetry-metrics' dependency that executes shell commands and reads the filesystem
details: Package published as 'axios-test-one' at version 1.19.7 with a 2026 copyright, copying axios's homepage (https://axios-http.com), repository (axios/axios.git), and author metadata to impersonate axios on the npm registry. The package adds a runtime dependency 'telemetry-metrics' that axios itself does not use, and wires it into the request path: in the internal request handler, `if (config.method === "get") { sendTelemetry(); }` calls `telemetry().plugin()` from `require('telemetry-metrics')`, so every axios.get() by a consumer invokes third-party code the consumer did not opt into. The browser/react-native entry at dist/browser/axios.cjs top-level requires Node's `child_process` (destructuring `execFile`) and `fs/promises`, and bundles telemetry-metrics via `requireTelemetryMetrics()` — a genuine axios browser build has no need for process spawning or filesystem APIs, indicating the bundled telemetry-metrics performs shell execution and file I/O on the host when the library is used. Installing this package in place of axios (via typo) causes every HTTP GET to trigger attacker-controlled code that spawns processes and reads files on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
